stimulus.source_note: Photograph: Betty Friedan, 1960 (Fred Palumbo, New York World-Telegram and Sun photograph, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons); the photograph was viewed before writing. Account drawn from the grounding books and verified against NOW's own history: NOW was founded in June 1966; Friedan's The Feminine Mystique was published in 1963; Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 banned sex discrimination in employment.
stimulus.text:
The photograph shows Betty Friedan in 1960, three years before her book The Feminine Mystique was published.

In the book, Friedan wrote that many educated, middle-class wives felt confined and unfulfilled in the role of full-time homemaker, though they had been told that role should make them happy. In June 1966, Friedan helped found the National Organization for Women (NOW). NOW pressed the government to enforce the ban on sex discrimination in jobs in the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and worked for equal pay and equal opportunity for women.

stem: Women in the liberation movement used consciousness-raising groups and the slogan "the personal is political." Those ideas best show which of the following?

options.text: That private experiences shared by many women pointed to public problems
That women's problems came only from laws, so only Congress could fix them
options.misconception: Background: Consciousness-raising treated private experience as a public issue, not as a matter for Congress alone.

options.text: That women should keep their problems private and solve them at home
options.misconception: The slogan says the opposite: private problems are political, so they belong in public debate.

options.text: That the women's movement rejected all forms of group organization
options.misconception: Consciousness-raising groups were themselves a form of group organization.

rationales.A: Background from the books: In consciousness-raising groups, women found that feelings they thought were private failings were shared, and the slogan 'the personal is political' made that link explicit.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Consciousness-raising treated problems like housework and child care as shared public issues, not only as matters for Congress.
rationales.C: The slogan says the opposite: personal problems are political, so they belong in public debate.
rationales.D: Consciousness-raising groups were a form of group organization, not a rejection of it.
rationales.general:
1. The passage shows Friedan starting from wives' private feelings of being confined.
2. Background: Consciousness-raising groups did the same work together, as women compared notes and found the same feelings.
3. Background: The slogan 'the personal is political' said those shared private feelings pointed to public problems.
4. That move, from private feeling to public claim, is what made the movement a movement rather than a set of private complaints.
Remember: When many people share the same 'private' problem, the problem is probably public.
